BEGIN WITH THE BIG QUESTIONS

How I read God, Jesus, the Bible and other religions.

What am I trusting? How do I read faithfully without making my interpretation untouchable? A personal essay about a Christian centre, honest disagreement and a love that remains answerable.

Read: Faith, with open hands →A personal essay · Open to correction

FOLLOW A THREAD INTO LIFE

Three ways to keep reading.

Move from interpretation into power, hope and the people close at hand. Each path has three short readings.

01 / POWER & SERVICE

Power that makes room

Ask what service would ask power to give up.

  1. If you could control everything, should you?

    Being able to control something does not settle whether you should.

  2. Leaving room is still a choice.

    Holding back can give someone room. It can also leave someone exposed.

  3. I can. May I? Should I?

    “Can I?”, “May I?” and “Should I?” are three different questions.

02 / HOPE & HONESTY

Hope without pretending

Leave uncertainty visible while remaining open to grace.

  1. Restoration without erasure.

    Hope for restoration does not require calling suffering good.

  2. Room for faith. Room for a question.

    This path explores a religious interpretation with its starting beliefs made clear.

  3. Let the correction leave a seam.

    When an explanation changes, leave a way to understand why.

03 / CARE & COMMUNITY

Love close at hand

Move from an account of care into an encounter with a person.

  1. Remember to care.

    Who or what needs my attention here?

  2. What are they trying to do?

    Before answering, ask what the other person is trying to do.

  3. Someone else can change the question.

    An outside reply can reveal a question we failed to ask ourselves.

The wider corpus remains open.
